definitions: To repeatedly hit or strike something until it is forced into a particular shape or place.
To instill or teach something to someone through persistent effort, often with difficulty or repetition.
To force entry into a place by breaking it down.
examples: He beat the metal into a new form.
They tried to beat some sense into him.
The police had to beat into the locked room.
pastTenses: beat into (past simple), beaten into (past perfect)
